TITLE: Investigating the Effects of Space-Variant Resolution on Object Representations
PROPOSAL: We will use the Xiph Monte Carlo Periphery Image simulation to generate a dataset with varying space-variant resolutions mimicking the human retina's sampling behavior, and then train a Time-Contrastive Learning (TCL) model on these representations. We will compare the TCL model's performance on recognizing objects from central vision versus peripheral vision, as well as how the performance changes when adding peripheral signals.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of TCL on this simulated dataset against a standard object recognition model trained on the full high-resolution field of view.
COST: 16 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the TCL model to perform significantly better on recognizing objects from central vision, but we might also observe improved performance in peripheral vision when incorporating signals from peripheral regions. If the simulation is too simplistic, our results might not generalize well to real-world settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Impact of Temporal Slowness on Object Representations
PROPOSAL: We will collect egocentric videos from the Egocentric Vision Dataset (EVD) and apply a temporal frame skipping strategy (e.g., only use every 3rd frame) to simulate human-like eye movements, resulting in videos with slower frame rates. Then, we will train a state-of-the-art SSL model on these processed videos and evaluate its performance on fine-grained visual categorization tasks. We will compare the results against the same model trained on full-rate videos.
CONTROLS: We will also ablate this experiment by training a model with random frame skipping and a model with a longer frame skipping period (e.g., every 5th frame) to evaluate the specific effect of slowing down the video rate.
COST: 24 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the model to perform better on fine-grained visual categorization tasks when trained on slowed-down videos, due to the increased attention to specific objects and scenes. However, we might also observe a decrease in overall performance due to the lack of contextual information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effects of Space-Variant Resolution and Temporal Slowness on Object Representations
PROPOSAL: We will train a robust SSL model on the space-variant resolution representations (from proposal 1) but with variable temporal rates (e.g., using 3 frames from normal videos and 1 frame from slow videos) to synthesize realistic head movements with space-variant information. This will allow us to investigate the joint effects of space-variant resolution and temporal slowness on object representations.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of this model against the models from proposals 1 and 2 separately, as well as against the standard SSL model trained on normal RGB videos.
COST: 48 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the performance to improve over the standard SSL model, especially for fine-grained visual categorization tasks, due to the combination of space-variant resolution and temporal slowness. However, the performance might be compromised if the variability in temporal rates causes inconsistent representations.
